explicit_validation.explanation: The paper conducts both LLM-as-a-judge evaluation (using GPT-4o to evaluate conciseness, coherence, and relevance) and human evaluation (focusing on factual errors), but never compares the results between the two methods. They evaluate different aspects on potentially different samples without any quantitative or qualitative comparison.

prompts.notes: The paper mentions prompting GPT-4o to score summaries on a 5-point scale for conciseness, coherence, and relevance, with more details in Appendix E.1, but exact prompts are not shown in the provided text.

guidelines.notes: Human evaluation guidelines include definitions of four factual error types (hallucination, particulars, predicate, entity) but detailed annotation instructions are not fully described.

criteria_mapping.notes: LLM and human evaluations focus on completely different aspects of summary quality - LLM evaluates general summary quality dimensions while human evaluation focuses specifically on factual accuracy/errors.
